original_value: Most electroencephalography (EEG) based emotion recognition systems make use of videos and images as stimuli. Few used sounds, and even fewer studies were found involving self-induced emotions. Furthermore, most of the studies rely on single stimuli to evoke emotions. The question of “whether different stimuli for same emotion elicitation generate any subject-independent correlations” remains unanswered. This paper introduces a dual modality based emotion elicitation paradigm to investigate if emotions can be classified induced with different stimuli. A method has been proposed based on common spatial pattern (CSP) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) to analyze human brain signals for fear emotions evoked with two different stimuli. Self-induced emotional imagery is one of the considered stimuli, while audio/video clips are used as the other stimuli. The method extracts features from the CSP algorithm and LDA performs classification. To investigate associated EEG correlations, a spectral analysis was performed. To further improve the performance, CSP was compared with other regularized techniques. Critical EEG channels are identified based on spatial filter weights. To the best of our knowledge, our work provides the first contribution for the assessment of EEG correlations in the case of self versus video induced emotions captured with a commercial grade EEG device.

result.paraphrase: Most EEG-based emotion recognition systems use videos and images as stimuli. Far fewer rely on sounds, and even fewer studies involve self-induced emotions. In addition, most studies depend on a single stimulus to trigger emotion. The question of whether different stimuli used to elicit the same emotion produce subject-independent correlations remains unanswered. This paper presents a dual-modality emotion elicitation paradigm to examine whether emotions induced by different stimuli can be classified. A CSP- and LDA-based method is proposed to analyze human brain signals for fear evoked by two different stimuli. One stimulus is self-induced emotional imagery, while the other uses audio/video clips. Features are extracted using CSP, and LDA is used for classification. Spectral analysis was conducted to investigate associated EEG correlations. CSP was also compared with other regularized techniques to improve performance. Critical EEG channels are identified from spatial filter weights. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first contribution assessing EEG correlations for self- versus video-induced emotions recorded with a commercial-grade EEG device.
